six_case_plan.positive: Run the exact owner-selected syntax route on these immutable source bytes. Expected ranges are authored from the pinned predicate, never observed output.
six_case_plan.negative: Run the independent valid alternative with this SAME rule active and require an enabled upstream descriptor even with no finding.
six_case_plan.configuration: Replay original positive bytes with the selected rule explicitly disabled. This is a separately counted configuration control, never a scope/default-activation reduction.
six_case_plan.version: Replay positive bytes under the pinned CLI; require a fresh per-cohort version probe and two per-rule Common/Native abstentions. Modeled baseline 2.4.21 versus parser 2.4.10 remains unqualified.
six_case_plan.suppression: Use genuine upstream file annotation only on an additional package-isolated copy; the unsuppressed original neighbor must keep every expected range.
six_case_plan.regression: Seal the negative correction as the child of suppression, delete the obsolete suppressed copy, and verify both registered parent and child unchanged.

bounded_predicate: Report eligible nonlocal val declarations at top level or in an object when the initializer is a recognized literal, a locally collected const-name text, supported arithmetic, or parentheses. Reject var/actual/getter/already-const/override, class instances and most annotations. Entity.atName(property). Explicit declared type and binding/effect/ABI validity are not checked. No rule-specific options.
selection_rationale: Adds storage/constant eligibility advice distinct from function-body and data-class mutability rules. Local scope, accessor semantics, declared nullable type and supported arithmetic demonstrate limits without resolving names or inventing a performance claim.

positive.intent: A top-level immutable primitive literal can be represented as a compile-time constant in a context where inlining/interoperability is intended; this remains explicit opt-in policy.

sources.Case.kt:
package corpus.maybeconstant

const val RETRY_LIMIT: Int = 3

negative.intent: A legal const val already expresses the intended compile-time value and must not report.

suppression.intent: Genuine file-scoped upstream suppression only on a package-isolated positive copy. The byte-identical unsuppressed Case.kt keeps all authored ranges; no host filtering or ktChecker-ID alias.

controls.intent: The literal initializer matches, but the explicitly nullable declared type is not permitted for const val. Keep this anticipated unsafe-advice false positive instead of treating the initializer as sufficient semantic proof.
A local immutable literal is legal code but cannot be declared const at local scope; the explicit local-property exclusion keeps it unreported.

sources.Case.kt:
package corpus.maybeconstant

const val BASE_LIMIT: Int = 1
val totalLimit: Int = BASE_LIMIT + 2

controls.intent: A same-file const name combined with supported arithmetic is recognized; the already-const BASE_LIMIT is not a second finding. No cross-file or overloaded-operator binding is inferred.

sources.Case.kt:
package corpus.maybeconstant

val retryLimit: Int get() = 3

controls.intent: An accessor-backed property is deliberately excluded even when its body returns a literal; property access behavior is a separate API surface.

limitations: Explicit nullable/non-primitive types can make a reported property invalid as const; source initializer shape alone is insufficient.
Const-name collection and the exact @JvmField annotation spelling are syntactic. Cross-file resolution, name collisions, all annotation aliases and object nesting are not comprehensively covered.
Inlining a public value can change binary compatibility and update behavior. No performance or interoperability benefit is measured, and no automatic rewrite is permitted by these data.

Local syntactic advice only. No binding identity, safe automatic rewrite, whole-program reachability, binary ABI compatibility, call effect, reflection completeness, performance or semantic qualification follows.

The six lifecycle cases include a disabled-rule configuration control, pinned-version positive replay and negative child-snapshot replay; the latter two are not new predicates. Every other negative/control keeps this rule active.

Only the existing explicit JVM LIGHT input is proposed. Common and Native requests must abstain without launching; no parser/compiler/Kotlin 2.4.21 versus embedded 2.4.10 compatibility or multiplatform qualification.
File-level suppression is authored; declaration-level aliases, baselines and generated-code inclusion policy are not newly qualified.
qualification_note: Authored expected ranges and concrete counterexamples come from primary source and language reasoning before execution, never detector outputs. Preserve any unexpected findings/misses and stop; do not rewrite oracles to force a pass. Existing activation/severity/certainty remain exact. Independent oracle/source review, root adoption, fresh controls and separately admitted single-cohort real isolated calls are required. No natural-project precision, safety, release or historical-stage transfer.
